name: D.O.A.
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Joey Shithead put the word "hardcore" on an album cover in 1981, then spent the next four decades touring it, and eventually ran for city hall.

eras.title: From the Skulls to a 500-copy single
eras.text: Joe Keithley came home from a failed Toronto trip with a new name and a band that started as a joke about Ramones records. Within months D.O.A. had a single, a San Francisco fan in Jello Biafra and a reputation for volume.

years.src: The Skulls (Canadian band) - Wikipedia · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories · Vancouver Magazine: Joey Shithead: Forever Punk
years.h: The Skulls die in Toronto; Joe Keithley comes home to start D.O.A.
years.p: The Burnaby band that switched from rock to punk after seeing the Ramones never made it out of Toronto, and Keithley formed D.O.A. in Vancouver.
years.xp:
The Skulls were Keithley, bassist Brian Goble, guitarist Simon Werner and drummer Ken Montgomery, who had all been in the rock band Stone Crazy. Wikipedia says they left Vancouver because the club circuit was mostly hostile and the only other punk bands were the Furies and the Dishrags. The Skulls made no records while active.

Keithley says Montgomery, known as Dimwit, is the one who told him to call himself Shithead, and the first name floated for the band was Joey Shithead And The Marching Morons. On the band name, Keithley told Punknews: "We always said the most famous D.O.A. was JFK." Vancouver Magazine reports that an earlier Keithley band's first paid gig, at the Grasslands Motor Inn in Merritt on June 5, 1977, ended with the manager firing them despite a signed contract for $500 over four nights.

years.cap: D.O.A. in their first year. Credit to be added.
years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories
years.h: First show at Vancouver's Japanese Hall, with a singer who can't keep time
years.p: Harry Homo fronted the lineup of Keithley, drummer Chuck Biscuits and bassist Randy Rampage. He was dismissed soon after for a lack of rhythm, and Keithley took over vocals.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says a guitarist called Randy Romance lasted through March 1978, and Brad Kent joined in June and was dismissed in September. Keithley has been the lead vocalist ever since, and the only constant member.

In the years since, the band has counted five bassists and roughly eight drummers, Keithley told the Dallas Observer.

years.src: Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Disco Sucks: 500 copies, paid for with unemployment cheques
years.p: The self-released EP was funded by Keithley's girlfriend's unemployment cheques, according to Punknews. Wikipedia says it topped the chart at San Francisco's KUSF.
years.xp: Keithley told Punknews the band recorded it in about eight hours, with the lyrics still being finished during the session. They mailed copies to record shops in California, New York, Chicago and Toronto, plus college radio stations.

years.cap: Mabuhay Gardens, San Francisco. Credit to be added.
years.src: Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Something Better Change - Wikipedia
years.h: Thrown out of Mabuhay Gardens for spraying beer; Biafra stops the show
years.p: Jello Biafra halted the show until Keithley was let back in, per Punknews. It was D.O.A.'s first San Francisco trip and the start of a long relationship with Biafra.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates D.O.A.'s first San Francisco shows to August 1978, at the Mabuhay. Biafra's Alternative Tentacles later issued the compilation Bloodied But Unbowed, reissued Something Better Change in 2002, and put out Last Scream of the Missing Neighbors with Biafra singing for D.O.A.

eras.title: Opening for the Clash
eras.text: A first North American tour, a manager, a second guitarist and one bad night at UBC. By 1980 the band had the lineup and the songs for a debut album.

years.cap: The Clash's October 1979 Vancouver date. Credit to be added.
years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · MONTECRISTO: That Time the Clash Played Soccer With a Bunch of Vancouver Punks
years.h: D.O.A. opens for the Clash at the Pacific Coliseum
years.p: The Clash's October 1979 tour stop in Vancouver put D.O.A. on a bill with a band they had grown up listening to.
years.xp:
Earlier that year, on January 31, 1979, the Clash played the Commodore and, before the show, took on local punks at soccer in a Vancouver park. Nick Jones of the Pointed Sticks told Montecristo: "They beat us... We lost 5-3." The players named include members of the Pointed Sticks, the Rabid, Corsage and the Subhumans.

D.O.A. had toured North America for the first time in May 1979, and afterward hired Vancouver journalist and activist Ken Lester as manager. Wikipedia says Dave Gregg joined as second guitarist late that year, and that a disastrous UBC Student Union Building show led Biscuits and Rampage to quit, replaced briefly by Andy Graffiti and Simon "Stubby Pecker" Wilde. Keithley took them both back in March 1980.

years.src: Something Better Change - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Something Better Change: three years of songs, two guitars
years.p: Recorded in Vancouver between 1977 and 1980 with producer Richard Drake, and released on Friends Records. Wikipedia notes it was out of print for nearly two decades.
years.xp:
Trouser Press describes the record as tighter than the band's earlier singles, with two-guitar arrangements. Sudden Death reissued it in 2000, Alternative Tentacles in 2002 with a re-recorded "Disco Sucks" added, and it came out again in 2011.

Critic Jack Rabid called the first two albums "revolutionary" and distinct from each other, and Ballast magazine ranked Something Better Change number 10 among its top 50 Canadian albums in 2013.

eras.title: The name goes on the cover
eras.text: Hardcore was a word a San Francisco magazine had been trying out; D.O.A. put it on a festival poster and then on an album. Within a year the rhythm section that made it was gone.

years.big: "We were the progenitors of spreading that name around"
years.src: Alternative Press: DOA discuss the legacy of second album 'Hardcore 81' · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A)
years.h: Black Flag drives north for a two-night festival called Hardcore 81
years.p: Section 8 filled in for 7 Seconds, who couldn't make it. Keithley, speaking to Alternative Press, on what the festival did for the term.
years.xp:
Keithley told Punknews that a San Francisco magazine article in late 1980 had used "hardcore" for bands including D.O.A., Black Flag and the Circle Jerks. When D.O.A. organised the festival in Vancouver, he named the album he was about to make after it.

Alternative Press dates the festival to February and March 1981; Punknews says March.

years.src: Alternative Press: DOA discuss the legacy of second album 'Hardcore 81' · Hardcore '81 - Wikipedia
years.h: Hardcore '81: eighteen minutes, one Led Zeppelin cover
years.p: Released April 22, 1981, it is credited with popularizing the word for the whole genre. Wikipedia lists Sudden Death as the label.
years.xp:
Producer Tracy Marks got a first side of eleven minutes and a second of seven, per Alternative Press. The songs were written alongside the debut's, and the record includes a Led Zeppelin cover, "Communication Breakdown", with Keithley singing an octave below Robert Plant under an underwater vocal effect.

On relistening after a remaster that fixed tape dropouts, Keithley said: "Fuck, this is a really good record!" In 2019 it won the public vote for the Polaris Heritage Prize.

years.src: Randy Rampage - Wikipedia · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Chuck Biscuits - Wikipedia
years.h: Rampage fired on New Year's; Biscuits leaves; Wimpy Roy arrives
years.p: Keithley dismissed bassist Randy Rampage after the New Year's Eve show. Drummer Chuck Biscuits left after a California tour, and Brian Goble joined as "Wimpy Roy", bass and second voice.
years.xp:
Dimwit, the Skulls drummer, moved to bass after Rampage went, then back to the kit when Goble arrived. Wikipedia says Biscuits left to join Black Flag; his own page says he played with them only briefly in 1982, after which conflict with Henry Rollins pushed him toward the Circle Jerks.

Biscuits later joined Danzig in 1987 on Rick Rubin's invitation and left in 1994 over royalty disputes. Rampage returned to D.O.A. for the 2002 album Win the Battle.

years.src: War on 45 - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A. · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories
years.h: War on 45: Bob Dylan, the Temptations and a reggae song
years.p: An eight-song 12-inch on Alternative Tentacles and Sudden Death, with covers of "Masters of War" and the Temptations' "War".
years.xp: Robert Christgau gave it an A-. Trouser Press likened the band's sound to a keyboardless Stranglers. Keithley told the Dallas Observer: "It has some straight up punk rock and a reggae song. I think the variety made it fun for everybody."

eras.title: Lawyers, hard rock and Biafra
eras.text: D.O.A. toured harder than anyone, went to Europe, tried to sound like a rock band and fought over who owned its records. The decade ended with a record fronted by Jello Biafra and a farewell show.

years.src: Squamish Five - Wikipedia · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Let's Wreck the Party - Wikipedia
years.h: Burn It Down: a single for the Vancouver Five's defence fund
years.p: Subhumans bassist Gerry Hannah was one of five anarchists arrested in January 1983. D.O.A. released a single to fund their defence.
years.xp:
The Squamish Five bombed a BC Hydro substation on Vancouver Island in May 1982 and moved 550 kg of dynamite toward Toronto's Litton Industries plant that October; the RCMP arrested them on January 20, 1983.

In a 1984 interview, Keithley said the single raised at least $2,500 and that he was a character witness at Hannah's sentencing, per Wikipedia. The song "Trial by Media" on Let's Wreck the Party is about Hannah.

years.src: Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A)
years.h: Bloodied But Unbowed: the primer for the first Europe tour
years.p: Alternative Tentacles compiled the first two albums and singles for D.O.A.'s first UK and European run, per Punknews.
years.xp: Keithley says he founded Sudden Death Records to keep control: "I thought this way I could put out what records I wanted whenever I wanted." The label released D.O.A. and also the Pointed Sticks and the Young Canadians.

years.src: Let's Wreck the Party - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A. · The Canadian Encyclopedia: D.O.A. · Punknews: Interviews: Joey Keithley (D.O.A) · The Big Takeover: You're D.O.A.! An Interview With Joey Keithley
years.h: Let's Wreck the Party: punk and hard rock, on purpose
years.p: Alternative Tentacles issued it to get ahead of a demo tape another label had obtained. It includes a cover of "Singin' in the Rain".
years.xp:
Producer Brian MacLeod helped the band lean into hard rock; the band felt hardcore had lost political relevance. "General Strike" had first appeared on the John Peel session EP, for striking British miners.

Trouser Press called it "a cutting and witty record". In the same year the Canadian Encyclopedia counts D.O.A. playing 105 cities in over a dozen countries, and Keithley told Punknews of a Leeds show where the PA lay on its side because the venue feared punks would knock it over. Staff locked up without turning off the beer taps, so the band helped themselves.

Keithley told The Big Takeover that a mid-1980s legal fight with a label cost $50,000 US, about $77,000 Canadian at the time.

years.src: Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · The Big Takeover: You're D.O.A.! An Interview With Joey Keithley
years.h: True (North) Strong and Free: fascism, Canada, a trumpet
years.p: Trouser Press hears Canadian identity and anti-fascist politics, with more instruments than D.O.A. had used before.
years.xp:
Drummer Kerr Belliveau lasted three weeks in 1986, recorded the Expo Hurts Everyone 7-inch and part of this record, and was replaced by Jon Card of Winnipeg's Personality Crisis, who stayed through 1990. Card died April 8, 2024, at 63; no cause was given publicly.

Keithley told The Big Takeover that he has recovered most of the band's early albums from labels, but that this one and Murder were still unavailable.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: D.O.A. fires manager Ken Lester; guitarist Dave Gregg leaves
years.p: Lester had managed the band since 1979. Chris Prohom of the Dayglo Abortions took Gregg's place.

years.src: Last Scream of the Missing Neighbors - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A.
years.h: Last Scream of the Missing Neighbors: Jello Biafra fronts D.O.A.
years.p: Six songs on Alternative Tentacles, produced by Biafra and Cecil English, including the 14-minute "Full Metal Jackoff".
years.xp:
Biafra sings; Keithley, Prohom, Brian Goble and Jon Card play. Trouser Press praised Biafra's "whiny" vocals against the band's "meat-and-cojones guitar power", and said it carries on the Dead Kennedys' work. It ends with a cover of "We Gotta Get Out of This Place".

"That's Progress" appeared on the Rock Against Bush, Vol. 1 compilation.

years.cap: The Commodore Ballroom, Vancouver. Credit to be added.
years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Trouser Press: D.O.A.
years.h: The "final" D.O.A. show, at the Commodore
years.p: Keithley announced in August 1990 that he was breaking up the band; promoter Dirk Dirksen suggested a West Coast farewell tour that ended in Vancouver.
years.xp:
The band's last album before the break was Murder in 1990, with a rawer sound that Wikipedia calls almost thrash metal. The live album Talk Minus Action Equals Zero came out afterward, while Keithley pursued acting.

Trouser Press describes the live album as the farewell record. D.O.A. stayed dormant for about 19 months.

eras.title: A three-piece with something to say
eras.text: D.O.A. came back with fewer people and a tougher outlook. Then it started losing friends, and the record it made in the middle of that is one of the strongest of its career.

years.big: "Kicking the establishment square in the groin"
years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Reunion: Keithley, Wimpy Roy and drummer Ken Jensen
years.p: Keithley's description to Exclaim! of what he thought no new band was doing. The reformed D.O.A. signed to Alternative Tentacles.
years.xp: Jensen, from the band Red Tide, was recommended by NoMeansNo's John Wright, who also produced the records and played keyboards. Exclaim! quotes Keithley as saying he wanted to combine "the obnoxious loud qualities with humour and social activism."

years.src: Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: 13 Flavours of Doom: John Wright behind the desk
years.p: Trouser Press credits the NoMeansNo drummer's production with bringing back "spunk and inspiration".

years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Dimwit, who told Keithley to call himself Shithead, dies
years.p: Ken Montgomery died in autumn 1994; Exclaim! reports a heroin overdose. That year keyboardist Ford Pier also joined on guitar.

years.src: Trouser Press: D.O.A. · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: The Black Spot, made after Ken Jensen's death in a house fire
years.p: John Wright drummed on the album. Alternative Tentacles put out a Ken Jensen memorial single with Red Tide.
years.xp: Trouser Press called it the band's tautest, most precise and hard-edged work, recorded amid the tragedy.

years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive · Brian Roy Goble - Wikipedia · Joe Keithley - Wikipedia · Exclaim!: R.I.P. Brian "Wimpy Roy" Goble of the Subhumans/D.O.A.
years.h: Wimpy Roy leaves after 14 years; Keithley takes over the bass
years.p: Brian Goble quit after the Black Spot tour. Exclaim! says he was frustrated with label issues.
years.xp:
Keithley played bass himself from 1996 to 1998, per Wikipedia. That same year he ran for the BC Green Party in a provincial election, as he did again in 2001, when he had the second-highest vote share among the party's candidates after leader Adriane Carr.

Goble later rejoined the Subhumans, and died of a heart attack on December 7, 2014, aged 57. Keithley called him "a humanist, a great father, an incredible singer and bass player."

eras.title: Bob Rock, Burnaby and a farewell
eras.text: A new drummer, an old bassist and a Metallica producer. Then Keithley went looking for a political job, and the band called it a day, for a while.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia · Exclaim!: D.O.A. Is Alive
years.h: Win the Battle: Randy Rampage is back after twenty years
years.p: Rampage played bass, then left again after the recording; Dan Yaremko took over.
years.xp: Exclaim! says Rampage rejoined for European and Japanese tours before going back to longshoring work. Wikipedia says Vancouver's mayor, Larry Campbell, declared December 21 D.O.A. Day in 2003 for the band's 25th anniversary.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Northern Avenger, produced by Bob Rock
years.p: Rock, known for his Metallica records, produced it. Rampage played on it but left before the tour.
years.xp: The 30th anniversary tour began in September 2008 with Dan Yaremko back on bass. Drummer the Great Baldini had left; James Hayden quit before recording and Floor Tom Jones took over.

years.src: The Globe and Mail: What happens when an old punk rocker enters politics · Dallas Observer: D.O.A.'s Joey "Shithead" Keithley on 35 Years of Punk Rock Memories · D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Keithley knocks on 2,000 doors and loses the NDP nomination by five votes
years.p: He was after the New Democratic Party nomination in Coquitlam-Burke Mountain. D.O.A. went on hiatus while he campaigned.
years.xp:
The Globe and Mail reported that Keithley, then 56, knocked on about 2,000 doors over two months. He told the paper: "I've been a student of politics since I was 14, 15, 16." The five-vote margin comes from the Dallas Observer.

D.O.A.'s farewell tour started January 18, 2013, at Vancouver's Rickshaw Theatre, with dates in BC, Alberta and California.

eras.title: Same name, new rhythm section
eras.text: The farewell lasted about twenty months. A new drummer and bassist arrived, a song named after a presidential candidate followed, and Keithley finally won an election.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: Farewell cancelled: D.O.A. re-forms with Paddy Duddy and Mike Hodsall
years.p: Keithley posted the news on the Sudden Death Records site. An October Canadian tour supported the live album Welcome to Chinatown.
years.xp: Dave Gregg, the guitarist from 1979 to 1988, also died in 2014, Wikipedia says.

years.src: D.O.A. (band) - Wikipedia
years.h: A single called "Fucked Up Donald"
years.p: D.O.A. aimed the April 2016 release at Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump.

years.src: Invisible Oranges: D.O.A. Still Prepared To "Fight Back" After Four Decades
years.h: Fight Back: the 17th studio album takes on inequality
years.p: Keithley told Invisible Oranges that inequality was the record's central theme.

years.src: Randy Rampage - Wikipedia
years.h: Randy Rampage dies at 58
years.p: Wikipedia cites reports that he died at his Vancouver home of an apparent heart attack. He played on the first two albums and returned twice.

years.cap: Joe Keithley, Burnaby Green Party. Credit to be added.
years.src: Exclaim!: D.O.A.'s Joe Keithley Elected to Burnaby City Council · Joe Keithley - Wikipedia
years.h: Keithley wins the last seat on Burnaby city council by 215 votes
years.p: Exclaim! says the Green Party win broke the Burnaby Citizens Association's monopoly on the council.
years.xp: Keithley won the eighth and final seat with 15,745 votes. He had run as a Green in 2013, 2015 and 2017, taking 13.77% in the 2017 Burnaby-Lougheed provincial race, per Wikipedia. He was re-elected in 2022, and on December 15, 2025, Wikipedia says, he switched to the Burnaby Citizens Association.
